who: Historian of early America at West Virginia University; PhD Syracuse University.

evidence.says: WVU identifies Mary Lou Lustig as committee chair of Thomas Edward Carney’s 2001 history PhD dissertation on the King’s College controversy, matching the listed student and title.
The history faculty list names Mary Lou Lustig among the emeriti and gives her doctorate as Syracuse University.
LC identifies Mary Lou Lustig through her books on Robert Hunter and New York’s provincial elite, consistent with the supervisor’s early American field.

notes: Full name, doctorate institution, field and directly documented 2001 supervision agree.

who: University of Connecticut historian of modern US political culture, gender and memory; PhD NYU, 2003.

evidence.says: UConn’s history profile gives McElya’s NYU PhD in 2003, an Alabama appointment in 2003–2008 before UConn, and authorship of Clinging to Mammy.
LC establishes Micki McElya as the author of Clinging to Mammy (2007), the same book listed on her UConn faculty profile.

notes: The exact doctorate and faculty history match; the shared book connects the LC candidate to the UConn historian.

who: Donald J. Pisani, historian of the American West and water policy at Oklahoma; PhD UC Davis, 1975.

evidence.says: Oklahoma’s 2009–2011 catalog lists Donald J. Pisani, PhD California at Davis in 1975, and history professor emeritus, with appointment in 1990 and emeritus status in 2010.
UC Press identifies Donald J. Pisani as Oklahoma’s Merrick Professor of History and lists his books From the Family Farm to Agribusiness and To Reclaim a Divided West.
LC identifies Donald J. Pisani through those same two books, connecting the authority candidate to the Oklahoma professor.

notes: Doctorate institution and year match exactly; Oklahoma affiliation and shared works establish the identity.

who: US labor historian formerly at the University of Mississippi, now Missouri; PhD Northwestern, 2006.

LC establishes Jarod Roll as the author of Spirit of Rebellion (2010), the same work listed in the institutional biography.

who: Catherine E. Rymph, historian of modern US policy and women at Missouri; PhD University of Iowa.

Tulane names Susan Schroeder as committee chair for Jonathan Truitt and Richard Conway in 2009 and Mark Lentz in 2008, all listed students.

who: Charles G. Steffen, historian of early America and urban history at Georgia State; PhD Northwestern.

evidence.says: Georgia State identifies Ruediger as a 2017 history PhD; he states that Charles Steffen advised his dissertation, directly matching a listed student.
The University Press of Kentucky’s repository record identifies Charles G. Steffen as a Georgia State history professor and author of The Mechanics of Baltimore.
LC connects Charles G. Steffen, also catalogued as Charles George Steffen, to The Mechanics of Baltimore and the 1977 dissertation Between Revolutions.
Georgia State’s 1995 catalog lists Charles G. Steffen as professor of history with a Northwestern doctorate.

notes: The student testimony establishes supervision; the university and publisher records connect the fuller candidate name and doctorate to that supervisor.
